strings.d1.s0.name: Peak Tram
strings.d1.s0.tips: The first trams at 07:30 have no queue. It's an 8-minute ride to Victoria Peak, around 88 HKD return.
strings.d1.s1.name: Victoria Peak Sky Terrace 428
strings.d1.s1.tips: Terrace at the summit with 360° views of the harbour. The morning haze burns off.
strings.d1.s2.name: Peak Circle Walk
strings.d1.s2.tips: A flat, shaded 3.5 km walk around the summit with great views.
strings.d1.s3.name: Tim Ho Wan Central
strings.d1.s3.tips: The cheapest Michelin-starred dim sum in the world. Don't miss the BBQ pork buns (char siu bao).
strings.d1.s4.name: Central Mid-Levels Escalator
strings.d1.s4.tips: The world's longest outdoor covered escalator system. It takes you up to SoHo and Tai Kwun.
strings.d1.b0.name: Lan Fong Yuen
strings.d1.b0.tips: A cha chaan teng (Hong Kong-style café) open since 1952. Try the milk tea and the pork chop sandwich.
strings.d1.b1.name: Tai Kwun
strings.d1.b1.tips: A former police station and prison, now a free cultural centre.
strings.d2.s0.name: Star Ferry Central Pier
strings.d2.s0.tips: The legendary 8-minute ferry from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui. 5 HKD with an Octopus card.
strings.d2.s1.name: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade
strings.d2.s1.tips: The Avenue of Stars and harbour views. Good for morning photos.
strings.d2.s2.name: Hong Kong Museum of Art
strings.d2.s2.tips: An art museum on the waterfront. Free entry, with Chinese calligraphy and contemporary art.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mak's Noodle Jordan
strings.d2.s3.tips: The classic wonton noodles. The bowls are small, so order 2.
strings.d2.s4.name: Temple Street Night Market
strings.d2.s4.tips: Fortune tellers, street food and cheap goods. It comes alive after 18:00, so try the claypot rice.
strings.d2.b0.name: Australia Dairy Company
strings.d2.b0.tips: Scrambled egg toast and steamed milk pudding. The queue moves fast.
strings.d2.b1.name: Kowloon Park
strings.d2.b1.tips: A park in Tsim Sha Tsui with flamingos. An alternative to the museum.
strings.d3.s0.name: Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
strings.d3.s0.tips: A 25-minute cable car ride from Tung Chung (around 300 HKD return, glass-bottom cabin extra). You get views of the sea and mountains.
strings.d3.s1.name: Tian Tan Buddha
strings.d3.s1.tips: A 34 m bronze Buddha. Climb the 268 steps for views over Lantau.
strings.d3.s2.name: Po Lin Monastery
strings.d3.s2.tips: The monastery at the foot of the Buddha. Vegetarian meal tickets are sold here.
strings.d3.s3.name: Po Lin Vegetarian Restaurant
strings.d3.s3.tips: The monastery's vegetarian kitchen. Simple and tasty.
strings.d3.s4.name: Tai O Fishing Village
strings.d3.s4.tips: A village of stilt houses. A boat trip (with a chance of spotting pink dolphins) costs 30 HKD, and there's a dried fish market.
strings.d3.b0.name: Tai O Dried Seafood Market
strings.d3.b0.tips: Grilled seafood in Tai O. An alternative to the monastery meal.
strings.d3.b1.name: Wisdom Path
strings.d3.b1.tips: A path of wooden sutra pillars next to the Buddha. A short walk.
strings.d4.theme: Mong Kok and Sham Shui Po
strings.d4.s0.name: Chi Lin Nunnery
strings.d4.s0.tips: A Tang-style wooden nunnery built without nails, with lotus ponds.
strings.d4.s1.name: Nan Lian Garden
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Chinese garden opposite the nunnery, with a golden pagoda.
strings.d4.s2.name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
strings.d4.s2.tips: Fortune sticks (kau cim) and incense. The busiest temple in Hong Kong.
strings.d4.s3.name: Kwan Kee Bamboo Noodle
strings.d4.s3.tips: In Sham Shui Po, noodles kneaded with a bamboo pole. Legendary flavour.
strings.d4.s4.name: Sham Shui Po Apliu Street
strings.d4.s4.tips: An electronics and fabric market in Hong Kong's most local neighbourhood, with street food.
strings.d4.b0.name: Tim Ho Wan Sham Shui Po
strings.d4.b0.tips: The first Tim Ho Wan branch.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ladies' Market Mong Kok
strings.d5.s0.name: Dragon's Back Trail
strings.d5.s0.tips: Hong Kong's most famous ridge hike (2 hours, easy to moderate). It has views of Shek O and is ideal in winter.
strings.d5.s1.name: Stanley Market
strings.d5.s1.tips: A market in a seaside town. Good for silk and souvenirs.
strings.d5.s2.name: The Boathouse Stanley
strings.d5.s2.tips: Seafood on the Stanley waterfront, with a terrace.
strings.d5.s3.name: Stanley Promenade
strings.d5.s3.tips: Murray House and the seafront. Stop for a coffee.
strings.d5.s4.name: Shek O Village
strings.d5.s4.tips: The village where the ridge hike ends. There's a beach and a Thai restaurant.
strings.d5.b0.name: Stanley Plaza Food Court
strings.d5.b1.name: Deep Water Bay
strings.d5.b1.tips: A quieter bay next to Repulse Bay.
strings.d6.s0.name: Yung Shue Wan Lamma
strings.d6.s0.tips: Take the Macau ferry (1 hour, around 180 HKD) to see the Ruins of St. Paul's and Senado Square. You need your passport.
strings.d6.s1.name: Lamma Family Trail
strings.d6.s1.tips: A walk taking in A-Ma Temple and Taipa Village.
strings.d6.s2.name: Ruins of St. Paul's
strings.d6.s2.tips: The church facade that symbolises Macau. Portuguese heritage.
strings.d6.s3.name: Lord Stow's Bakery Macau
strings.d6.s3.tips: Portuguese-style pastel de nata (custard tart). A Macau classic.
strings.d6.s4.name: Senado Square
strings.d6.s4.tips: A mosaic-paved square with Portuguese buildings. The return ferry to Hong Kong leaves at 18:00.
strings.d6.b0.name: Taipa Village Food Street
strings.d6.b1.name: Macau Tower
strings.d6.b1.tips: A tower with bungee jumping and views over Macau.
strings.d7.s0.name: Hong Kong Park
strings.d7.s0.tips: A park among the skyscrapers, with an aviary and a lake.
strings.d7.s1.name: Ding Ding Tram Line
strings.d7.s1.tips: Ride the historic double-decker tram to Wan Chai. Take a front seat on the upper deck, 3 HKD.
strings.d7.s2.name: Kam's Roast Goose Wan Chai
strings.d7.s2.tips: Michelin-starred goose. A farewell lunch, with a 30-minute queue.
strings.d7.s3.name: Airport Express Hong Kong Station
strings.d7.s3.tips: The airport train takes 24 minutes. You can check in in the city.
strings.d7.b0.name: Joy Hing Roasted Meat
strings.d7.b0.tips: Cheap char siu in Wan Chai.
strings.d7.b1.name: Blue House Wan Chai
strings.d7.b1.tips: A blue historic building and neighbourhood museum. An alternative to the tram.
strings.note0: The Octopus Card works everywhere (MTR, tram, ferry, shops). Buy it at the airport. The Airport Express takes 24 minutes.
strings.note1: October to December is the best season (22°C, dry). In January and February it's 15°C, a cardigan is enough and it's ideal for walking.
strings.note2: Dim sum is eaten in the morning and at lunchtime. Queues are normal at cheap Michelin spots like Tim Ho Wan and Kam's Roast Goose.
strings.note3: Tipping is not expected, and a 10% service charge is added to the bill. Cash is still common, and small restaurants don't take cards.
strings.note4: The Star Ferry and Peak Tram are Hong Kong rituals. Go up to the Peak at 08:00, and return at 19:00 for the evening lights.
strings.note5: You need your passport for Macau. Ferries to Lamma and Cheung Chau leave from Central Piers 4 and 5.
strings.transit.name: Octopus Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: It works on the MTR, trams, buses, the Star Ferry and in shops, so it covers everything in Hong Kong.
